This is the converse of what we derived. The converse of an implication is not logically equivalent to the original implication.

Counterexample: Suppose W is true (woman buys the newspaper) but O is false (officer doesn't hate the food). This could happen if F is true for some other reason. This scenario doesn't violate either premise but makes the conclusion false.
